items.title: S&P 500 falls, dragged down by Nvidia sell-off and rate-hike fears after hot inflation data
items.take: Tuesday's session closed lower as the hot CPI print and hawkish Fed talk sank tech, with Nvidia the worst offender. Overnight, UBS's Americas CIO came out against the half-point jumbo, saying a quarter-point December hike is the realistic path, while Asia opened lower tracking Wall Street.

items.title: Stocks Drop as Rate-Hike Worries Rise: Stock Market Today
items.take: Stocks opened lower Tuesday and never recovered, with strategists calling the hot headline and core prints proof that inflation is stickier than consensus presumed, likely cementing a December hike. Core CPI has now run 0.3% three months straight, and Wedbush doesn't expect the Huang scandal to cost the Nvidia CEO his job despite removal chatter.

items.title: US market ends lower as hot inflation data, Fed comments heighten rate worries
items.take: Nvidia slid 5.5% as several firms cut price targets in the wake of the CEO scandal and Trump said the FBI is investigating. Albion Financial's Jason Ware called the jumbo-hike panic 'irrational,' pinning six months of CPI pressure on oil, energy and diesel pushing through.

items.title: Goldman Sachs now expects the Federal Reserve to hike in March as well as in December
items.take: After the hot print, Goldman dropped its call that December would be the Fed's last hike: economist David Mericle now adds another quarter point in March 2027 and pushes the first cut all the way back to December 2027. The peak lands at 4.25% to 4.5%, from 3.75% to 4% today.

items.title: Tech Stocks Rebound Even As OpenAI Logs Heavy Losses
items.take: Today's rotation pick, fresh this Wednesday morning: chip names are bouncing back even as OpenAI's heavy losses make the rounds, and the show covers where the December-hike debate settled overnight.
